query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.mechanism: reduction of defects and improvement of material properties through optimized process parameters
generation.predicted_outcome: improvement in dimensional precision and mechanical integrity by 15% relative to the current fabrication baseline

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the optimized process parameters do not result in a 10% improvement in dimensional precision and mechanical integrity, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: In order to determine the optimal process parameters, namely laser power P, scanning speed v, and powder feeding rate q, for the laser cladding of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, microhardness HV, dilution rate η, and aspect ratio W/H were selected as the evaluation criteria for the cladding quality. The dilution rate η can be represented using the melting area of the substrate (Am) and the cladding area (Ac), which is calculated as Am/(Ac + Am), or simplified as h/(H + h). Regions Ac and Am are shown in Figure 2. Gray correlation theory is a robust approach for analyzing the intrinsic correlation between uncertainty and ambiguity data, offering high accuracy and stability in data processing []. Therefore, this theory was employed to investigate how each process parameter affected cladding quality.
The constraint conditions are the ranges of various processing parameters in the laser cladding experiment of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy, as shown in Equation (9).
